findings.title: Each flusher process creates its own SpansBuffer for shared Redis keys, duplicating memory metrics and buffer views
findings.body: Previously there was a single SpansBuffer shared across the whole flusher; now `_create_process_for_shards` creates a separate `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process, and `self.buffers` holds one buffer per process. In `submit()`, `get_memory_info()` is now summed across these per-process buffers instead of a single buffer covering all assigned shards. If `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns info per-Redis-cluster-node (not per-shard), this can double count memory usage from shared Redis nodes across multiple shard subsets, causing incorrect backpressure decisions (false positives for max-memory backpressure) once more than one process is used.

findings.title: join() does not kill processes that fail to stop before deadline per-process
findings.body: In the new join loop, if the first process doesn't terminate within the deadline, the while loop exits due to deadline but `process.terminate()` is still called unconditionally afterward only for that process; however, for subsequent processes in the dict iteration, `remaining_time <= 0` immediately breaks the outer for-loop, skipping termination entirely for any processes not yet checked. This could leave live child processes without being terminated when timeout is tight and there are multiple flusher processes, causing dangling processes/resource leaks.

findings.title: max_processes can be None-derived shard-count larger than available shards silently clipped without validation of flusher_processes=0 or negative
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a passed `max_processes=0` the same as `None` (falls back to shard count) due to Python truthiness, which may be surprising/undesired behavior if a caller intends zero flusher processes (though zero wouldn't make sense, the silent coercion from invalid config to default behavior could mask a configuration bug).

findings.title: Test changed to require transactional DB without justification
findings.body: test_basic was changed from `@pytest.mark.django_db` to `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)`. This increases test cost/slowness and signals a new reliance on real transactions (likely due to multiprocessing in the flusher), but there's no comment explaining why, which can confuse future maintainers running into flaky/slow tests.
